source: walk-forward backtest of 2026-09-25 (106 companies, out of sample 2025-10-01 to 2026-09-04, after costs); raw per-trade results in docs/backtest/trades.csv

positive_trial.why: only 3 out-of-sample trades: too few to judge (needs 30 to judge, 50 to pass)

insider_buy_cluster.why: failed the strict bar: 32 trades (needs 50), not significant after correction; p = 0.240, 1.000 after correcting for 21 comparisons

contract_win.why: no backtest trades: needs a news archive to test, so it is judged on live outcomes (50 needed)

m_and_a_target.why: only 2 out-of-sample trades: too few to judge (needs 30 to judge, 50 to pass)

upgrade.why: no backtest trades: needs a news archive to test, so it is judged on live outcomes (50 needed)

confidence_check.plain: Higher confidence did WORSE (lower win rate and lower average return) for: top 10 vs the rest; 80+ vs 65-80. The confidence score does not rank trades and must be rebuilt before it is used for anything, including 'top signals' displays. With only 10 trades the top-10 row alone proves nothing either way; the 65-80 vs 80+ comparison has more trades.

bar: ON only with >= 50 trades that beat the S&P 500 over the same days (win rate, average return, Sharpe) and p < 0.05 after a Bonferroni correction; >= 30 trades and failed = OFF; fewer than 30 = unproven
